chunks: Muhammad b. Ahmad al-Asadi narrated to us. He said: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. al-Hasan al-Amiri narrated to us. He said: Ibrahim b. Isa b. Ubayd al-Sadusi narrated to us. He said: Sulayman b. Amr narrated to us from Abdullah b. Hasan b. Hasan b. Ali from his mother Fatima bt. al-Husayn from her father, peace be upon him. He said: The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and his family, said:
Indeed, the rectification of the beginning of this nation is through asceticism and certainty, and the destruction of its end is through stinginess and wishful thinking.

key_terms.الأمل: Amal — wishful thinking, false hopes; excessive attachment to worldly ambitions that distracts from the hereafter
key_terms.الزهد: Zuhd — asceticism, detachment from worldly excess; one of the cardinal virtues in Islamic spirituality
key_terms.الشح: Shuhh — stinginess, miserliness; considered worse than regular bukhl as it implies withholding even what is due to others
key_terms.اليقين: Yaqin — certainty of faith, firm conviction in God's promises and the unseen

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the causes of success and failure of the Muslim nation?
ai.summary: This prophetic tradition, transmitted through the family of the Prophet via Fatima bt. al-Husayn, presents a concise diagnosis of communal health. The Prophet (s) teaches that the early Muslim community thrived through zuhd (detachment from worldly excess) and yaqin (firm faith), while later generations would decline through shuhh (miserliness) and amal (false hopes and endless worldly ambitions). This reflects a common prophetic theme about the moral trajectory of the Muslim umma.
